results.title: Korean Neocloud Firms Race to Raise Cash for GPUs - Seoul Economic Daily
highlights:
■Investors Line Up Amid AI Boom Mondrian AI Secures 20 Billion Won VESSL AI Seeks 200 Billion Won More Elice Group Turns to IPO for Funding GPU Shortage Blocks On-Demand Inquiries Focus on Supply Chains and R&D

Published 2026.09.30. 17:36:49

By Kim Ji-young jikim@sedaily.com

ClipArt Korea

South Korean neocloud companies are accelerating fundraising to secure graphics processing units (GPUs) and expand cloud infrastructure. As surging demand for artificial intelligence computing draws investor interest, these firms are raising their funding targets or pursuing follow-on rounds. With the proceeds going into supply chain expansion and operating technology development, competition to secure a stable GPU supply is expected to intensify.

...

VESSL AI, which closed its own Series B round earlier this year, is now recruiting additional investors. The current round targets 200 billion won. The company is valued at 500 billion won, and some observers expect it to reach 1 trillion won next year. The business is growing quickly, with revenue projected to rise to about 100 billion won this year from 3 billion won last year. VESSL AI has secured roughly 7,000 GPUs and aims to hold 10,000 by year-end.

...

These companies are focused on raising cash because the neocloud market is growing rapidly as the spread of generative AI drives explosive demand for high-performance GPUs. Neocloud firms secure GPUs in bulk, supply them to companies on demand and provide environments optimized for AI computing. Citing that competitive edge, research firm Gartner has projected that neocloud providers will account for 20% of an AI cloud market expected to be worth $267 billion in 2030. Against that backdrop, Korean firms are moving to seize the opportunity and take the lead in the business.

In Korea, too, GPU supply is failing to keep pace with demand. Some neocloud companies are finding it difficult even to accept inquiries about on-demand services, which let customers rent GPUs as needed. Supply is already tight enough to meet demand from customers seeking large-scale, long-term GPU use.

As a result, competition among neocloud companies to secure GPUs is expected to intensify. Korean firms plan to put the money they have raised into expanding GPU supply chains and into research and development on GPU interconnection and operation. VESSL AI and Mondrian AI in particular run their cloud businesses with most of their GPUs secured through contracts with outside suppliers and companies. That is why the ability to secure GPUs is seen as a key variable separating winners from losers. Mondrian AI linked up with CoreWeave and Nebius as GPU suppliers this year. VESSL AI secured more than 1,000 B200 units through SK Telecom (017670) in August.

An official in the startup sector said Korean neocloud companies have until now competed mainly on price, offering the lowest rates at about half the cost of general-purpose cloud providers. "Now what will matter is the ability to stably operate GPUs scattered across multiple locations, along with AI services," the official said.

results.title: GPU rental prices in 2026: what moved and why — Strata GPU
highlights:
# GPU rental prices in 2026: what moved and why

Market 30 Sep 2026 6 min read

H100 rates fell to $1.70 an hour in late 2025 and climbed back above $3 by September 2026. What that swing means for anyone buying compute.

Few prices in technology moved as much as GPU rental rates over the last three years. Understanding the cycle helps you decide when to lock in a rate and when to stay flexible.

## 2023–2024: scarcity

After ChatGPT, demand for H100s outran supply. Hyperscaler on-demand rates sat around $7–8 per GPU-hour and lead times for clusters ran to months.

## 2024–2025: the glut

New datacenters came online, and many buyers who had reserved capacity found they needed less of it. Marketplace rates fell steadily, and one-year contract prices reached a low of about $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025, according to SemiAnalysis.

## 2026: tight again

Inference and media-generation demand absorbed the surplus faster than expected. By March 2026 roughly half of providers had no on-demand H100 stock, and capacity coming online through the summer was booked in advance. The Silicon Data H100 rental index stood at $3.06 in September 2026.

## What it means for buyers

- Lock rates for steady workloads. When the market is tight, a reservation buys availability as much as a discount.
- Keep bursts flexible. On-demand capacity for experiments avoids committing at the top of a cycle.
- Don't buy hardware to escape the cycle. Owners of GPUs bought in 2023 watched their rental value fall by about three quarters before it recovered.

Sources: SemiAnalysis, Silicon Data, public provider pricing.

results.title: Huurprijs voor Europese GPU-capaciteit stijgt tot 21 procent - MSP Business
highlights:
# Huurprijs voor Europese GPU-capaciteit stijgt tot 21 procent

30 september 2026, 12:02 Door Redactie

Nebius verhoogt per 1 oktober 2026 zijn uurprijzen voor het huren van GPU-capaciteit met 17 tot 21 procent. Dat blijkt uit de maandelijkse Europese GPU-prijsindex van onderzoeksbureau Lindstead. Volgens dezelfde index huur je een NVIDIA H100 bij Europese aanbieders nog steeds voor ongeveer de helft van de prijs bij AWS en Microsoft Azure.

De prijsverhoging bij het in Amsterdam gevestigde Nebius geldt voor meerdere GPU-generaties. Een NVIDIA H100 gaat van ongeveer €3,38 naar €3,95 per uur ($3,85 naar $4,50). Voor de B300, de nieuwste generatie, stijgt het uurtarief van ongeveer €6,88 naar €8,33 ($7,85 naar $9,50).

Lindstead plaatst de verhoging in een bredere ontwikkeling. Volgens het bureau is de mediane huurprijs van een H200 in twaalf maanden met ongeveer 25 procent gestegen. Daarnaast constateert Lindstead dat elke nieuwe GPU-generatie per uur duurder is dan de vorige.

### Europese aanbieders onder hyperscalerprijzen

Uit de index blijkt dat Europese aanbieders een H100 op on-demandbasis verhuren voor ongeveer de helft van de prijs bij AWS en Microsoft Azure, en voor ongeveer een derde van het tarief bij Google Cloud. Het Franse OVHcloud rekent volgens de index ongeveer €2,62 per uur, het Finse Verda €3,09 en Nebius vanaf 1 oktober €3,95. Scaleway uit Frankrijk vermeldt prijzen vanaf €2,73 per uur.

Bij de Amerikaanse hyperscalers liggen de uurtarieven voor een H100 hoger. AWS rekent €6,03, Microsoft Azure €6,12 en Google Cloud €9,71 per uur.

Lindstead baseert de cijfers op de prijspagina’s van de aanbieders en op getdeploying.com, geraadpleegd op 27 september 2026. Dollarprijzen zijn omgerekend tegen de ECB-referentiekoers van 25 september 2026 (1 euro = 1,1403 dollar). De vergelijking betreft openbare on-demandprijzen. Tarieven bij reserveringen, langlopende contracten of maatwerkafspraken kunnen afwijken.

...

De Europese GPU-prijsindex vergelijkt maandelijks de openbare on-demandprijzen van Europese en Amerikaanse cloudaanbieders voor de NVIDIA H100, H200, B200 en B300. Per aanbieder vermeldt de index ook het hoofdkantoor en de eigenaar. Lindstead geeft aan geen commissies van aanbieders te ontvangen.

results.title: Episode 01: Compute Markets | The Knowledge | General Index
highlights:
## Our key takeaways

### 1) Compute is already a commodity. What it lacks is a mature market

David puts compute trading at around $1tn a year, already roughly a third to half the size of oil trading. The surprising thing is that the physical market has reached that scale before the financial infrastructure around it has really developed. There isn’t yet a liquid futures market giving you a forward curve or an obvious market price to fall back on. That makes pricing compute harder – but also makes a credible index unusually valuable.

### 2) The index isn't just measuring a market... it's helping to make the market possible.

The scale of the market and the lack of clear data draws the value of good indexes and consistent methodology into clear relief. Benchmarks give the market something to price against, settle against and ultimately build financial products around. Compute Desk and General Index are helping to make this market possible.

### 3) Compute is technologically novel, but the market dynamics are familiar.

Different GPUs, network configurations and clusters make compute messy to compare, but crude has grades, power has locations and delivery periods, and plenty of other commodity markets started out highly bilateral and fragmented. The most unusual thing about this market is the speed at which it is being built.

...

Neil: AI is causing a massive expansion in demand for compute. How is the market evolving?

David: "Something that people don't realise is that the markets are massive. They are already massive. When people talk about it being the new oil, they probably refer to the fact that we estimate that people are trading — that is, buying and selling hours on a GPU — at the scale of about a trillion dollars a year."

"And that's not very far from the scale of oil markets, which are around two to three trillion dollars a year. So this is already happening. A lot of it is obviously being bought by the hyperscalers, but there's a huge amount that is being bought by other companies."

The distinction that follows is the crux of the whole episode:

"They already exist in the physical sense. People are buying compute, they are selling compute. In the financial sense, those financial markets do not exist. There are not very many derivatives being traded, and when they are, they're being traded over the counter, OTC, in bilateral deals that people are doing because they want to hedge their exposure — effectively transfer your risk."

...

David: "In any market where you're trading an asset, if you want to trade that asset massively and without bilateral deals, you need some level of standardisation. And there is some level of standardisation. An H100 is not sold for the same price as an H200."

"But there is a lot more that goes into that standardisation — whether that's the connectivity between the GPUs, the network access. When people trade, they don't really trade a GPU, they trade a cluster. So there are a lot of dimensions across that cluster that need to be taken into account, and that creates difficulties in developing this market."

...

David: "The biggest challenge is also the most exciting thing, which I would say is that it's a moving target. Things are moving very fast. There is a huge amount of demand."

"But we have to remember that commodity markets in other asset classes and commodities were built over a period of twenty, thirty years — and we are trying to accelerate that, to build them over a period of two and three years. It's a hard thing to do."

"There are lots of functions of the markets that do not exist, and you need to create them, or try to facilitate or partner with people to create them."

That compression is the defining feature of compute as a market story. Crude took decades to move from bilateral contracts to benchmark-settled futures. Compute is attempting the same arc inside a single hardware cycle, while the underlying asset itself keeps changing generation.

results.title: AI Demand Diverges: Token Usage Soars, H100 Falls While B200 Rebounds, DRAM Drops After Five Straight Gains | BTCC
highlights:
JPMorgan's latest report reveals deep fractures in the AI infrastructure market: September token usage surged 71% month-over-month and 30x year-over-year, but prices were cut in half year-over-year, as cheap open-source models like DeepSeek and GLM reshape the industry with a "volume over price" strategy. Meanwhile, H100 rental prices turned lower, and DRAM prices fell for the first time after five consecutive gains, signaling mounting supply expansion pressure beneath the surface of the compute market's boom.

Overall AI infrastructure demand remains strong, but price signals across market segments are clearly diverging. According to JPMorgan's latest data center observation report, September token usage and spending both accelerated, but GPU rental prices moved in opposite directions, and memory spot prices declined for the first time after a sustained rally.

According to the trading desk, JPMorgan analyst Joseph Cardoso noted in a September 29 report that September token usage on the OpenRouter platform surged 71% month-over-month and 30x year-over-year, with overall spending up 28% month-over-month and 14x year-over-year.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's GPU rental market showed clear divergence: A100 and H100 rental prices both fell month-over-month, while B200 rebounded slightly after its first decline in August. In the memory market, DRAM spot prices saw their first slight month-over-month decline in September after five consecutive months of gains, while NAND prices were essentially flat.

These signals carry complex implications for AI infrastructure investors. The continued acceleration in token usage confirms the authenticity of AI application-layer demand, but downward pressure on GPU rental prices and the pause in memory price gains suggest that supply expansion and shifting demand structures are constraining hardware pricing.

...

## GPU Rentals: H100 Under Pressure, B200 Stabilizes and Rebounds

September's GPU rental market for non-hyperscale cloud service providers showed clear divergence. According to Bloomberg index data, the average A100 rental price was $1.59 per GPU hour, down 2.8% month-over-month, a larger decline than August's 0.7%; the average H100 rental price was $2.64 per GPU hour, down 2.6% month-over-month, compared to a 0.4% increase in August.

B200 moved in the opposite direction. September's average B200 rental price rebounded to $5.70 per GPU hour, up 1.3% month-over-month, reversing August's 1.5% decline. The B200-to-H100 price ratio rose to 2.16x (from 2.08x in August), and the H100-to-A100 price ratio also edged up to 1.66x (from 1.65x in August).

JPMorgan noted that B200 pricing is about 2.2x that of H100, and H100 pricing is about 1.7x that of A100, with both ratios rising month-over-month, reflecting that the relative premium for next-generation compute is being maintained, but supply pressure on older GPU models is intensifying.

highlights:
2026-09-30 12:21

### 摘要： 综合指数今日收15.777元/卡·时、较前一交易日上行0.24%，19条基准价报价全部持平。采价侧两条规模化信号：H200云南一批45台三年闭口资源公开挂牌15.7万元/台·月，来自居间渠道、机主端约15万元；5090青海一批128台现货以年租形态入市，报价1.48万元/台·月。高端侧可锁定资源仍紧、消费级侧批量供给宽松，可获量差异成为价格支撑的主要分水岭。

【市场概述】

SMM算力租赁价格综合指数今日收于15.777元/卡·时，较前一交易日上行0.24%，为连续第二个交易日小幅上行；19条基准价报价较前一交易日全部持平。采价侧同日出现两条规模化放租信号：高端H200云南一批45台三年闭口资源公开挂牌，报价15.7万元/台·月；消费级5090青海一批128台现货以年租形态入市，报价1.48万元/台·月。

【H200：云南45台三年闭口挂牌15.7万，居间渠道非直报】

9月29日某居间渠道在行业交流群公开挂牌，出租一批H200 SXM 141G整机（8卡口径）共45台，机房位于云南，闭口三年，现货可测，报价15.7万元/台·月。该报价为公开挂牌口径、来源为居间渠道而非机主直报，剔除居间费用后对应机主端约15万元/台·月。45台为近期公开渠道单次放租量较大的H200现货之一。对照9月下旬某渠道一批64台三年闭口资源在广东以13.5万元/台·月成交，两批在渠道来源、机房地区与配置口径上均不同质，不具直接可比性。

【5090：青海128台以年租入市，报价1.48万】

某算力服务商9月29日就一批5090整机资源给出报价：现货128台，单机配置2T内存，机房位于青海，报价1.48万元/台·月，租期以年租起、倾向三年闭口合同，支持按需拆分。同期另一批5090资源（3台、湖北机房）以短租形态报1.45万元/台·月，仅接受月租或最长半年闭口。两批在台数、内存配置与租期条件上均不同质，报价差异不具直接可比性。

【SMM观点】

今日两条线索同处供给放量一侧、指向不同。SMM认为，H200三年闭口在居间渠道以15.7万元挂牌，与9月下旬同条件成交的13.5万元之间仍有约2.2万元的挂牌—成交距离，反映居间加价与卖方锁价诉求同时存在，可锁定资源的稀缺性尚未松动；5090这一侧则以128台批量、年租起、支持拆分的形态入市，供给端的批量弹性明显强于高端侧。两端合看，当前高端H200与消费级5090在可获量上的差异，正在成为价格支撑的主要分水岭——H200的报价韧性来自可租资源的有限，5090的批量供给则削弱了短期议价空间，这一分化值得持续跟踪。
